findings.title: Missing prisma import causes runtime ReferenceError
findings.body: File uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but there is no import of @calcom/prisma in the file. Any Salesforce calendar operation calling getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar functionality.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token fetched but never used
findings.body: After refreshing and persisting new tokens, the returned jsforce.Connection is constructed from the old credentialKey.instance_url/accessToken/refreshToken instead of accessTokenParsed.data. The refresh network call therefore has no effect and the client continues to use the expired access token.

findings.title: Refresh error check uses statusText instead of ok/status
findings.body: Code checks response.statusText !== "OK" to detect refresh failure. Fetch statusText is implementation-dependent and often empty, so failures can be missed or successes incorrectly rejected. Should check !response.ok or response.status.

findings.title: Minimum token schema is invalid and strips required fields
findings.body: The schema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to literal strings such as "[object Object]", not a catch-all. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so validating an external sync response with this schema will drop expiry/refresh fields or fail unexpectedly. Should use .passthrough()/.catchall() instead.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token replaced with dummy string
findings.body: If the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code mutates it to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers then persist this to credential.key, permanently corrupting the stored credential with a non-functional refresh token.

findings.title: Sync path returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response, but Google (expects res.data), Hubspot (expects token object), and Zoho Bigin/CRM (expects axios response with .data) callers treat the result as their original library type. For example Google does res?.data which is undefined for a fetch Response, causing TypeError on token.access_token. The helper needs to normalize shapes or callers must handle both.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId where the userId parameter is expected, so the sync endpoint receives calcomUserId equal to the credential ID, not the user ID. The remote lookup will fail or return another user's token.

findings.title: Unvalidated request handling allows method abuse and 500s
findings.body: Handler has no HTTP method check so GET/PUT also create/update credentials, and z.object.parse plus JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt are called without try/catch. Invalid bodies, malformed encrypted payloads, or wrong encryption keys throw uncaught and return 500 instead of 400, and expose stack traces.
